subject: History
description: Shah Jahan (1628-1658) — Mughal emperor of Taj Mahal, Mumtaz Mahal, Peacock Throne, Shahjahanabad (Old Delhi), war of succession.

questions.stem: TAJ MAHAL was built by SHAH JAHAN in memory of:
questions.explanation: TAJ MAHAL — built 1632-1648 by Shah Jahan in memory of his FAVOURITE WIFE MUMTAZ MAHAL (Arjumand Banu Begum), who died in 1631 giving birth to their 14th child. LOCATION: AGRA, on the banks of YAMUNA. ARCHITECTS: USTAD AHMAD LAHAURI (chief architect); design influenced by Persian, Islamic, Indian styles. WORKERS: ~20,000 craftsmen, 1,000+ elephants for hauling materials. COST estimated at ~32 million rupees of the time (~hundreds of crores in today's money). MATERIALS: WHITE MAKRANA MARBLE from Rajasthan; semi-precious stones inlaid (PIETRA DURA technique) — jasper, jade, sapphire, turquoise, amethyst. UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE 1983; one of NEW SEVEN WONDERS OF THE WORLD (2007 vote). SYMMETRY: perfectly mirrored along central axis; main mausoleum, mosque, jawab (response building), gardens (charbagh). FOUNTAINS, REFLECTING POOL, GARDEN. RECENT (2024): visited by ~7-8 million people/year; major source of foreign exchange for India tourism. TAJ MAHAL TRIVIA: appears to change colour through the day — pinkish at dawn, white at noon, golden at sunset, silvery at moon-light. PRESERVATION: pollution from Mathura refinery, leather tanneries threatened the marble (yellowing); protective measures since 1990s. PYQ FREQUENCY: Taj-Mumtaz link is a 1-mark guarantee in SSC, UPSC, MPSC.

questions.stem: SHAH JAHAN's famous PEACOCK THRONE (Takht-e-Tawus) was looted by which invader?
questions.explanation: PEACOCK THRONE (Takht-e-Tawus) — golden throne commissioned by Shah Jahan, completed 1635 after 7 years of work; encrusted with thousands of precious stones (including the original KOH-I-NOOR diamond, on the throne in early years). VALUE: estimated at ~1 crore rupees of the time — comparable to TWICE the cost of Taj Mahal. NADIR SHAH — Persian emperor — invaded India in 1739; defeated Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah at the BATTLE OF KARNAL (Feb 1739); LOOTED Delhi for 57 days; carried away the PEACOCK THRONE + KOH-I-NOOR + tons of gold/silver/gems back to Persia. The Mughal treasury was DEPLETED — ~70 crore rupees taken (gigantic for that era). AFTERMATH: Mughal empire NEVER recovered economically; rapid decline post-1739. NADIR SHAH was assassinated 1747; the Peacock Throne was BROKEN UP and parts dispersed across Persia/Afghanistan/India. KOH-I-NOOR ('Mountain of Light') diamond — passed through many hands: Mughals → Nadir Shah (named it 'Koh-i-Noor') → Ahmad Shah Abdali → Punjab's Maharaja Ranjit Singh → seized by British 1849 (Treaty of Lahore) → presented to Queen Victoria 1850. NOW set in Queen Mother's crown (UK Royal Treasury). REPATRIATION DEMANDS: India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Iran all claim. PYQ FREQUENCY: Nadir Shah-Peacock Throne in SSC, UPSC, MPSC — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: SHAH JAHAN built which new capital city, including the famous RED FORT?
questions.explanation: SHAHJAHANABAD — capital city established by Shah Jahan in 1648, after he moved his court from Agra to Delhi. Now part of OLD DELHI. KEY STRUCTURES BUILT: (1) RED FORT (Lal Qila) — completed 1648; UNESCO Heritage. Made of red sandstone; key buildings inside: Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience — held the Peacock Throne), Naubat Khana, Rang Mahal, Mumtaz Mahal, Khas Mahal. (2) JAMA MASJID — INDIA's LARGEST MOSQUE; built 1650-1656; capacity 25,000+ worshippers; opposite Red Fort. (3) CHANDNI CHOWK — main bazaar street; designed with a CANAL flowing down its middle (filled in by British). (4) MOTI MAHAL, BARI BAOLI, FATEHPURI MASJID. INDEPENDENCE DAY ceremonies: PM addresses nation from Red Fort ramparts each 15 August (since 1947); Republic Day Parade (Jan 26) on Rajpath, ends near India Gate. SHAHJAHANABAD vs NEW DELHI: SHAHJAHANABAD is OLD DELHI; New Delhi was built by British (1911-1931, Lutyens & Baker design) — separate planned city. URBAN SHAHJAHANABAD: ~6 sq km original walls; today merged into massive Delhi metropolis (NCT). PYQ FREQUENCY: Shahjahanabad-Red Fort in SSC, UPSC, MPSC, NCERT 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Shah Jahan's reign is often called the 'GOLDEN AGE' of Mughal:
questions.explanation: SHAH JAHAN's REIGN (1628-1658) — universally regarded as the ARCHITECTURAL ZENITH of the Mughal era. KEY ACHIEVEMENTS: (1) TAJ MAHAL (Agra, 1632-48). (2) RED FORT (Delhi, 1639-48). (3) JAMA MASJID (Delhi, 1650-56). (4) Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) at Agra Fort. (5) Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace, Lahore). (6) Wazir Khan Mosque (Lahore). (7) Shalimar Gardens (Lahore, Kashmir). (8) Restoration/extension of Akbar's Agra Fort. STYLE: marriage of Persian, Islamic, Indian architecture; emphasis on white MARBLE, intricate INLAY WORK (pietra dura), perfect SYMMETRY, geometrical gardens (charbagh). UNESCO HERITAGE SITES from his era: Taj Mahal (1983), Red Fort (2007), Agra Fort (1983), Lahore Fort (1981 — in Pakistan). MILITARY: also significant — recovery of Kandahar (1638, but lost again 1648), Deccan campaigns, but military expansion was less than father Akbar. RELIGIOUS POLICY: more orthodox than Akbar but not as harsh as Aurangzeb. ECONOMIC: empire's WEALTH at peak; GDP estimates ~25% of world's GDP under Shah Jahan. RUIN: by his last years, Mughal economy strained by lavish architecture costs + wars + son's rebellion (Aurangzeb 1657-58). DEATH: 1666, while imprisoned in Agra Fort by Aurangzeb (since 1658). Buried in Taj Mahal next to Mumtaz. PYQ FREQUENCY: Shah Jahan-architecture link in SSC, UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: WHO imprisoned Shah Jahan in Agra Fort during the WAR OF SUCCESSION?
questions.explanation: AURANGZEB — Shah Jahan's THIRD son — emerged victorious in the WAR OF SUCCESSION (1657-1658), imprisoned his father, and ascended throne as Mughal Emperor. SHAH JAHAN'S 4 SONS: (1) DARA SHIKOH (eldest, ~1615-1659) — heir-apparent; LIBERAL, scholar, translated Upanishads to Persian (Sirr-e-Akbar); FAVOURED by Shah Jahan. (2) SHAH SHUJA (~1616-1660) — Governor of Bengal; rebellious. (3) AURANGZEB (Mohi-ud-din, 1618-1707) — Governor of Deccan; orthodox, ruthless military strategist. (4) MURAD BAKHSH (~1624-1661) — Governor of Gujarat; weaker. WAR OF SUCCESSION (1657-58) — sparked when Shah Jahan FELL ILL (1657); rumors he was dying. KEY BATTLES: (1) Battle of DHARMAT (April 1658) — Aurangzeb defeated imperial forces. (2) Battle of SAMUGARH (May 1658) — DECISIVE; Aurangzeb crushed Dara Shikoh near Agra. (3) Aurangzeb captured Agra Fort (June 1658), imprisoned Shah Jahan. (4) Aurangzeb crowned himself July 1658 at Shahjahanabad. (5) Pursued and KILLED Dara Shikoh (Aug 1659, Delhi). (6) Eliminated brothers Shuja, Murad. SHAH JAHAN's FATE: imprisoned in Agra Fort (Musamman Burj — view of Taj Mahal); cared for by daughter JAHANARA. Died 1666. AURANGZEB ruled 1658-1707, expanded Mughal empire to greatest extent but seeds of decline. PYQ FREQUENCY: war of succession in SSC, UPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: DARA SHIKOH, Shah Jahan's eldest son, is famous as a:
questions.explanation: DARA SHIKOH (1615-1659) — Shah Jahan's eldest son, heir-apparent. PHILOSOPHIC LIBERAL: deeply interested in Hindu philosophy, Sufism, comparative religion. WORKS: (1) MAJMA-UL-BAHRAIN ('Mingling of the Two Oceans') — comparative essay on Hinduism and Islam, finding common ground. (2) SIRR-E-AKBAR ('Great Secret') — Persian translation of 50 UPANISHADS (Hindu philosophical texts); MAJOR cultural milestone — gave Europe access to Hindu philosophy via Persian → Latin (Schopenhauer cited it). (3) Translated YOGA-VASISHTHA, BHAGAVAD GITA into Persian. (4) Wrote SAFINAT-UL-AULIYA on Sufi saints. PHILOSOPHY: believed Hinduism and Islam were SAME core truth in different forms; sought religious harmony — much like his great-grandfather AKBAR. POLITICAL OPPONENTS: orthodox ulema (Muslim clergy) viewed him as HERETIC — fueled their support for AURANGZEB (orthodox). DEATH: defeated at Samugarh (1658), captured 1659, executed by AURANGZEB on charges of HERESY (Aug 1659, Delhi). His tomb is in HUMAYUN'S TOMB COMPLEX. LEGACY: 'WHAT IF DARA HAD WON?' is a famous historical counterfactual; some scholars argue Mughal empire (and India) might have evolved differently — more pluralistic, possibly delayed colonial collapse. RECENT: efforts to rehabilitate Dara Shikoh's image in modern India (street renaming, exhibitions). PYQ FREQUENCY: Dara Shikoh in UPSC History optional, modern history.

questions.stem: Which architect is credited as the chief designer of the TAJ MAHAL?
questions.explanation: USTAD AHMAD LAHAURI — credited as the CHIEF ARCHITECT of the Taj Mahal. He was an Iranian-origin engineer-architect; led a team of designers including Mir Abd-ul-Karim, Makramat Khan, and others. STYLE INFLUENCES: (1) Persian / Timurid mausoleum tradition (Gur-e-Amir in Samarkand, Humayun's Tomb in Delhi). (2) Islamic geometric symmetry. (3) Indian craftsmanship, jali (latticework). (4) European decorative motifs (introduced through Mughal court). EARLIER MUGHAL ARCHITECT FAMILY: HUMAYUN'S TOMB (built 1565-72 by his widow Hamida Banu, designed by Mirak Mirza Ghiyas) is considered the PROTOTYPE of Taj Mahal architecturally — same charbagh garden, central dome, symmetric layout. ITIMAD-UD-DAULAH'S TOMB (1622-28, Agra) — built for Nur Jahan's father; called 'BABY TAJ' for its pietra dura precursor. THESE EARLIER WORKS led to Taj Mahal's perfection. EUROPEAN MYTH: 17th-century European traveller Manucci speculated GERONIMO VERONEO (Italian) designed Taj — DISCREDITED. Indian and Muslim architects led the design. WORKERS: 20,000+ workers (master craftsmen from across the empire — Bukhara, Persia, Italy for stones), thousands of masons + 1,000 elephants. CONSTRUCTION: 1632-48. UNESCO HERITAGE 1983. PYQ FREQUENCY: Taj Mahal architect in UPSC History optional, NCERT 1× per 2 cycles.
